findings.claim: The fill-the-checklist control's failure text, and README Troubleshooting (line 208), diagnose every control failure as 'the 200px is coming from something around the tag (a wrapper, a float, columns or positioning)'. The control also fails a tag whose own width is right but whose own display shrinks to fit: probes on a private copy of the completed work showed a tag given display inline-block or table fails task 11 on that control with exactly this wrapper/float/columns/positioning message, while display flow-root and flex pass. For inline-block and table nothing around the tag is involved, so the feedback points the learner at the wrong cause. Pack 'tags' invite chip-style inline-block styling, and README task 11 only says 'ordinary blocks', a term the task never defines (the box-model topic page speaks only of 'normal block layout' when it discusses margin collapse). The narrowing itself is fair for this objective (it keeps the box-model calculation on the tag) and the README does state it; the gap is that the stated reason and the failure feedback do not cover the most likely way a learner breaks it, which costs retry time inside an already tight timing estimate. Graded high, on the same reading of the rubric as cl3-edu-002: a learner-facing claim is false for this case. Troubleshooting's 'the 200px is coming from something around the tag' is untrue for an inline-block or table tag. The solved-run record's variantRuns sentence, that the inline-block and floated variants failed 'as README task 11 and Troubleshooting state', repeats the claim for inline-block.
findings.recommendation: In the control's failure message and in README Troubleshooting, name the tag's own display as a cause alongside the surroundings: for example, say that inline-block, table-style display or a float make the tag shrink to its text, and that the tag must keep the default block display (or another display that fills the line). Optionally say in README task 11 Outcome what 'ordinary block' means (the default display of the starter's paragraph tags).

findings.claim: The solved-run record carries claims that its own rewritten fields contradict. 'privateStaging' says the solution 'existed only in the private $TMPDIR copy of the export during the run', and 'contract' says the run was 'exercised on a fresh pep export-lab bundle'. But 'procedure' says the lab was taken by git archive into a fresh private directory, not exported, and 'cleanup' says the private copy, completed starter files included, 'stays only in uncommitted private staging', so it did not exist only during the run. These fields were carried over unchanged from the previous record. 'environment.os' (macOS Darwin 25.6.0) is also carried over and cannot be checked from here; the reviewing machine runs Darwin 27.2.0. The core claims do hold: every artifactHashes entry matches the bytes at 0e12a9f7, and my own runs give a starter of 12 failing tests with the failing set equal to lab.json failingTests, and a solved run of 12 passing whose timing-masked output matches expected/on-completion.txt byte for byte. Graded high because the brief's rubric lists 'a claim is false' as high, and these false sentences are about where the private solution material lives and how long it stays there.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite 'contract' and 'privateStaging' to describe the run that actually happened (git archive into a private directory; the completed files remain in uncommitted private staging until retired). Re-record 'environment.os' from the machine that ran it, or mark it unverified. Do not change the hashes or the result.

findings.claim: The Tasks preamble says 'each TODO task comment in the sign-up corner of index.html marks the element that task changes'. index.html now also has a 'TODO task 11' comment in the gear checklist, which marks two tags the learner must keep and not change in markup. This sentence describes neither its location nor its purpose. Separately, README task 11 says the tags need a '3px solid border', but the test accepts any visible border style; a probe with a dashed border passed. That is harmless leniency but is not stated.
findings.recommendation: Say in the preamble that index.html also has a task 11 TODO in the gear checklist, which marks tags you style in styles.css and keep in place. Either drop 'solid' from the outcome or say only the border width is checked.

findings.claim: The timing stays labelled as an authoring estimate and its parts add up (5 + 28 + 12 + 8 = 53, cap 60 inside the 62-minute S21 slot), so it is honest. But it is tighter than before. The README grew from 2652 to 3218 words (about 21% more) at this change while the README-reading share stays at about 5 minutes. The median-to-cap buffer fell from 10 to 7 minutes, and the cap now sits only 2 minutes under the slot. Task 11's 8 minutes leaves little room for a retry after the control failure in cl3-edu-001 or for the hand-run box-model view check in 'Check it in a browser'.
findings.recommendation: Either state in lab.json notes that task 11's 8 minutes include reading its README section and the box-model view check, or re-derive the README-reading share for the longer README. Keep the cap inside the 62-minute slot.
